text:
1. The chapter's pivotal sentence concerns God's inner life.
2. Yahweh sees that every imagination of the human heart is only evil continually.
3. Yahweh is sorry that he made man.
4. Yahweh is grieved in his heart over humanity.
5. God's grief comes before the sentence of judgment.
6. God's grief gives the judgment its character.
7. The flood is driven by a maker's sorrow over what his creatures have become.
8. Before any rain falls, the first covenant in Scripture appears.
9. God promises to establish his covenant with Noah.
10. God tells Noah to enter the ark with his sons, his wife, and his sons' wives.
11. The covenant promise extends beyond Noah to the animals.
12. Two of every sort of animal are to be brought into the ark.
13. The promise includes provision of food to keep all of them alive.
14. The chapter that announces the end of all flesh also arranges in detail what will survive.
15. Noah is the one man who found favor with God.
16. Noah is told to gather in the creatures God is about to drown.
